methods.label: Square the radical side lengths
methods.explanation: The longest side is \(\sqrt{5}\). Since \((\sqrt{2})^2+(\sqrt{3})^2=2+3=5=(\sqrt{5})^2\), the converse of the Pythagorean theorem applies. It is a right triangle with hypotenuse \(\sqrt{5}\).
methods.levelReason: The grade 8 converse applies after using square-root identities and comparing positive square roots.
